question: After the focused cleanup repair, should OpenClaw permanently support this Discord configuration surface and a separate durable terminal progress lifecycle contract?
rationale: Automation can repair the stale-tracker bug, but maintainers must choose whether the optional Discord UX justifies seven settings, shared requester metadata, a channel adapter, and persisted generic run state.

options.title: Sponsor after repair and proof
options.body: Accept the direction only after the config-transition fix, conflict resolution, exact-head Discord proof, and explicit API review.

options.title: Narrow the lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep the Discord UX but refactor terminal cleanup to minimize separate generic persisted state or parallel lifecycle paths.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Close or defer the PR if maintainers do not want the long-term configuration and lifecycle commitment.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after repair and proof
recommendation.body: Accept the direction only after the config-transition fix, conflict resolution, exact-head Discord proof, and explicit API review.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history makes this the best available owner for the cross-cutting product and API choice spanning Discord, plugins, delivery context, and subagent lifecycle.
